proposals.title: Phosphorylation of NUP98 initiates nuclear-import failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy models of ALS
proposals.text:
Hypothesis title: Phosphorylation of NUP98 initiates nuclear-import failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy models of ALS.

This proposal tests one prespecified claim: in experimental TDP-43 proteinopathy, phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin NUP98 is an initiating nuclear-pore alteration that impairs selective nuclear import and thereby promotes nuclear TDP-43 depletion and neuronal dysfunction. The initiating event is covalent modification of NUP98. Nuclear TDP-43 loss, cytoplasmic TDP-43 assembly, and cell death are downstream responses that may also proceed in parallel. The claim is limited to TDP-43 proteinopathy models and TDP-43-positive ALS tissue. NUP62 and NUP153 stay separate hypotheses.

Supported premises. Disease-linked TDP-43 associates with insoluble nuclear-pore and transport components, disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in cell systems, and accompanies pore pathology in ALS tissue [S1]. This supports causal study of pore alteration while leaving the initiating chemistry unspecified [S1]. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can form independently of conventional stress granules, mislocalize transport-associated proteins, and coincide with impaired import, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and cell death [S3]. Phosphorylated TDP-43 in those assemblies is a TDP-43 modification, separate from nucleoporin phosphorylation [S3]. Expanded C9orf72 RNA is linked to RanGAP mislocalization and impaired import, and transport-directed manipulations can modify phenotypes in that genetic context [S2]. Cellular stress recruits transport factors into stress granules and impairs transport; altering stress-granule assembly can modify those defects [S4].

Speculative bridges. NUP98, the kinase, and the acceptor sites are assumptions. Unverified prior knowledge holds that NUP98 FG repeats contribute to the selective barrier and that mitotic CDK1 phosphorylates NUP98 at proline-directed sites during nuclear-envelope breakdown, loosening that barrier. The [S1] paraphrase supports nucleoporin mislocalization and does not name NUP98. The assumed bridge is that a proline-directed kinase, provisionally a CDK-family enzyme, places a partial analogous mark on NUP98 in post-mitotic neurons during TDP-43 proteinopathy. The prespecified neuronal effect is dual: FG-barrier compromise slows importin-mediated NLS import and raises passive permeability of an inert probe, while the Ran gradient and ATP stay intact at onset. Speculatively, mislocalization in [S1] may be phospho-dependent release of NUP98. Mitotic envelope breakdown is an analogy for barrier chemistry. Kinase action on NUP98 in stressed neurons remains an assumption until measured in the same model.

Alternative explanations. Stress granules may sequester transport factors so import fails while the pore stays covalently intact [S4]. Cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing may inhibit import directly and place pore changes downstream [S3]. Aggregates may displace nucleoporins, leaving later phosphorylation as a mark on damaged pores [S1]. C9orf72 repeat RNA and RanGAP mislocalization may explain import failure in that genetic context [S2]. Ran-gradient collapse or energetic failure can slow import with unmodified NUP98.

Discriminating preclinical test. Human iPSC-derived motor neurons with inducible disease-linked TDP-43, plus a matched stress paradigm that assembles stress granules in the absence of mutant TDP-43, are sampled densely around import onset. An enabling observation precedes any allele program in that exact model: proline-directed kinase activity by p-Rb and MPM2 reactivity, and NUP98 phospho-peptide abundance by deep phospho-enrichment plus targeted mass spectrometry, with site-specific antibody confirmation when reagents exist. Sites that rise on NPC-incorporated NUP98 before the import-kinetic decline, and the kinase whose activity rises in that same window, are nominated and locked before confirmatory experiments.

The locked pattern at onset is slower NLS-reporter import, higher passive permeability of a size-matched inert probe, and a preserved Ran nuclear-to-cytoplasmic gradient and cellular ATP. A Ran/ATP-controlled permeabilized import assay then supplies defined Ran, importin-β, and an ATP/GTP regenerating system to nuclei from the same cells. Persistence of the import defect after reconstitution supports an intrinsic phosphorylated-pore lesion. Restoration by those exogenous factors supports transport-factor shortage or energetic failure. Parallel readouts track G3BP1-positive stress granules, stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies, importin and RanGAP redistribution, and the nuclear-to-cytoplasmic TDP-43 ratio. Dense enrichment and targeted mass spectrometry reduce the chance of missing a sub-stoichiometric or transient mark.

Confirmatory alleles use endogenous editing of the locked NUP98 sites, or validated replacement that removes phosphorylatable endogenous NUP98. Targeted mass spectrometry must show loss of those phospho-peptides on NPC-incorporated NUP98, with normal baseline import and permeability, before any phenotype is interpreted. Prevention edits sites before phospho-onset; late rescue begins only after import has failed. A CDK-family inhibitor and genetic loss of the nominated kinase are read only together with the verified site edits, because CDKs modify many substrates. A crossed arm blocks stress-granule assembly while phospho-status, permeability, and import kinetics are measured independently. The same assay in C9orf72-repeat neurons tests whether a RanGAP-linked import defect [S2] requires the locked NUP98 mark.

Falsifying observation. After verified loss of the locked phospho-peptides on NPC-incorporated NUP98 and normal baseline transport, the initiating-site claim is falsified if pre-onset blockade leaves import-kinetic failure, the passive-permeability increase, and nuclear TDP-43 loss unchanged in timing and severity, or if the mark appears only after import has failed or only with insoluble TDP-43. Full restoration of NLS import by exogenous Ran, importin-β, and ATP/GTP despite the mark falsifies an intrinsic pore-chemistry cause. A phosphomimetic that leaves import and permeability intact weakens sufficiency. Failed late rescue after assemblies are present leaves initiation intact, because parallel downstream injury can persist. Import restored by stress-granule blockade despite the mark and altered permeability favors sequestration [S4].

Limitations. Kinase identity and sites lie outside [S1]–[S4] until the enabling observation assigns them. p-Rb and MPM2 report proline-directed activity and leave NUP98 substrate identity open until peptides are mapped. Phosphomimetics approximate phosphate. CDK perturbation is broader than one site. iPSC-neuron timing may differ from human disease chronology. Extremely brief marks can still be missed. The design tests a research hypothesis and does not validate a treatment.

proposals.title: Nup98 phosphorylation initiates selective nuclear-import failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy motor neurons before transport-factor sequestration
proposals.text:
Nup98 phosphorylation initiates selective nuclear-import failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy motor neurons before transport-factor sequestration

This proposal advances one testable hypothesis. In spinal motor neurons with TDP-43 proteinopathy, phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin Nup98 inside assembled nuclear pore complexes initiates selective nuclear-import failure. Depletion of nuclear TDP-43, growth of cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies, and sequestration of transport factors are downstream responses. The hypothesis applies to TDP-43 proteinopathy and is tested as a separate question in C9orf72-repeat neurons. A single mechanism for all ALS subtypes is outside the claim.

Supported premises are restricted to the packet. Disease-linked TDP-43 associates with insoluble aggregates that contain nuclear-pore and transport components, disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems, and occurs together with pore pathology in ALS tissue [S1]. Those findings support a connection between TDP-43 pathology and transport disruption. They leave the initiating chemistry unidentified and leave open other subtype sequences [S1]. Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA is linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons, and manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modify model phenotypes [S2]. This is a genetic-context-specific route. It supplies no direct nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism and no demonstration that sporadic ALS follows the same route [S2]. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can form independently of conventional stress granules, mislocalize transport-associated proteins, and accompany impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and cell death [S3]. Phosphorylated TDP-43 within those assemblies documents a modification of TDP-43, which is separate evidence from nucleoporin phosphorylation [S3]. The perturbations in that study do not establish every physiological ALS trajectory [S3]. Cellular stress recruits transport factors into stress granules and impairs nucleocytoplasmic transport, and altering stress-granule assembly modifies transport defects and disease-model phenotypes [S4]. Placed beside [S3], that sequestration route shows that conventional stress granules are not required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect [S4].

Speculative bridges are stated as assumptions. The modified subunit is Nup98. A proline-directed kinase that becomes active during TDP-43 pathology phosphorylates Nup98. The residues are unknown until they are mapped in the same motor neurons. Phosphorylated Nup98 binds nuclear transport receptors less effectively, and selective NLS-cargo import slows. Unverified prior knowledge from outside the packet is that phosphorylation of FG-nucleoporins can remodel pores during mitosis in non-neuronal cells. Using that analogy for post-mitotic ALS motor neurons is speculative. [S1] through [S4] do not name a kinase, a residue, or a Nup98 interaction.

Alternative explanations are tested alongside the hypothesis. A sequestration explanation holds that stress granules capture transport factors and thereby impair import [S4]. In that account, Nup98 phosphorylation is a coincident stress mark. A de-mixing explanation holds that cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies inhibit import and deplete nuclear TDP-43 without conventional stress granules [S3]. A secondary-injury explanation holds that nucleoporin mislocalization [S1] and RanGAP mislocalization [S2] follow broader cellular stress, so phosphorylation appears after transport has already failed. A genotype-restricted explanation holds that C9orf72 repeat RNA and RanGAP redistribution [S2] impair import through a route that leaves Nup98 unmodified.

The discriminating preclinical test uses order of appearance and reciprocal perturbation in human iPSC-derived spinal motor neurons. Isogenic TDP-43 proteinopathy cultures, C9orf72-repeat cultures, and matched controls are sampled from the earliest inducible window through the start of neuronal death. Measured events are Nup98 phosphorylation on isolated nuclear envelopes, the rate of NLS-reporter import, RanGAP localization, the nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio of TDP-43, G3BP1-positive stress granules, and localization of importins and Ran. Candidate residues are mapped by phosphoproteomics in these neurons before genome editing. Phospho-deficient Nup98, altered only at mapped sites, tests necessity inside the disease models. Phospho-mimetic Nup98 introduced into control neurons tests sufficiency without a disease transgene. An orthogonal block of stress-granule assembly tests the sequestration explanation [S4]. Support for initiation requires three observations: phospho-Nup98 appears before NLS-import failure and before G3BP1 granules; phospho-deficient Nup98 preserves NLS import and nuclear TDP-43; and phospho-mimetic Nup98 impairs import in control neurons that still lack stress granules. Support for sequestration is restoration of import by the stress-granule block while Nup98 phosphorylation stays high [S4]. Support for the de-mixing route is import failure that continues to follow cytoplasmic TDP-43 after Nup98 phosphorylation is prevented [S3].

Falsifying observation. In the TDP-43 proteinopathy motor neurons, the hypothesis is false if NLS-import failure and nuclear TDP-43 depletion occur without an increase in phosphorylation at the mapped Nup98 sites. It is also false if a stress-granule block or a cytoplasmic-assembly intervention restores import and nuclear TDP-43 while phospho-deficient Nup98 does not. An effect present only in C9orf72-repeat neurons would limit the claim to that genotype [S2].

Limitations. Kinase identity, residue choice, and selection of Nup98 remain assumptions. Phosphomimetic alleles approximate regulated phosphorylation. iPSC motor neurons omit aging, glia, and neuromuscular circuits. The packet does not validate this mechanism or any treatment.

proposals.title: Phosphorylation of FG-nucleoporin NUP98 initiates selective nuclear-import failure before nuclear TDP-43 loss in experimental TDP-43 proteinopathy
proposals.text:
Phosphorylation of FG-nucleoporin NUP98 initiates selective nuclear-import failure before nuclear TDP-43 loss in experimental TDP-43 proteinopathy

In neuron and cell models that express disease-linked TDP-43, phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin NUP98 is hypothesized to be an early intrinsic change in the nuclear pore complex. The phosphorylated pore weakens selective nuclear import. Loss of nuclear TDP-43 and later neuronal dysfunction follow that import failure. NUP98 phosphorylation is hypothesized to be temporally separable from recruitment of transport factors into stress granules. The claim is limited to experimental TDP-43 proteinopathy. C9orf72-linked disease and sporadic ALS are boundary conditions for comparison, and the same sequence is not assumed for every ALS subtype.

Supported premises come only from the packet. Insoluble TDP-43 aggregates associate with nuclear-pore and transport components. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental systems, and related pore pathology is present in ALS tissue [S1]. Those findings support a TDP-43-pore connection. They do not identify a nucleoporin phosphorylation event or place any such event first in the sequence [S1]. Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA alters RanGAP localization and impairs nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons, and manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms can modify model phenotypes [S2]. This is a genetic-context-specific route to transport failure and does not establish a nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism [S2]. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can form independently of conventional stress granules, mislocalize transport-associated proteins, and accompany impaired import, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death [S3]. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulates in those assemblies; that modification is on TDP-43 and is not evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation [S3]. Cellular stress can also sequester transport factors in stress granules and impair transport, and altering stress-granule assembly can modify transport defects and disease-model phenotypes [S4]. Together, [S3] and [S4] document two routes to a similar transport phenotype: granule-independent TDP-43 assemblies and granule-dependent sequestration.

Speculative bridges are explicit assumptions. No supplied source names NUP98, a kinase, or a phospho-site. Unverified prior knowledge, outside this packet, holds that FG-nucleoporins such as NUP98 contribute to the selective barrier and that CDK-family kinases phosphorylate nucleoporins when pores are remodeled in mitosis. The hypothesis assumes that a stress-responsive CDK-family activity places an analogous mark on NUP98 in post-mitotic neurons and that the mark is sufficient to reduce karyopherin-mediated import. The relevant residue is unknown and must be mapped. This bridge is not evidence.

Causal order. The initiating event is increased phosphorylation of NUP98 on assembled pores, preceding measurable loss of nuclear TDP-43. The downstream response is failed selective import, depletion of nuclear TDP-43, growth of cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies, and neuronal dysfunction [S1, S3]. Phosphorylation of TDP-43 within those assemblies is interpreted as a later marker [S3]. Stress-granule sequestration of transport factors [S4] and C9orf72-linked RanGAP mislocalization [S2] remain alternative or context-specific routes and are not required steps in the proposed TDP-43 chain. A further alternative is that the phosphate and the import defect are parallel consequences of broader cellular stress, so the two can correlate while the phosphate is unnecessary for the transport failure.

Discriminating test. In human iPSC-derived neurons with a disease-linked TDP-43 variant, and in an inducible cytoplasmic TDP-43 system aligned with [S3], compare isogenic controls across a time course that starts before nuclear TDP-43 loss. Identify the earliest NUP98 phosphosite by mass spectrometry. At physiological expression, introduce a non-phosphorylatable NUP98 allele and a separate phosphomimetic allele at that site, without altering stress-granule scaffolds. In a crossed arm, prevent stress-granule assembly with a perturbation of the type that modifies transport when sequestration is causal [S4], leaving NUP98 intact. At matched time points, quantify NUP98 phosphorylation, nucleoporin localization, a nuclear-import reporter, nuclear versus cytoplasmic TDP-43, transport-factor occupancy of stress granules, and neuronal survival. Add a C9orf72-repeat neuron arm [S2] solely to ask whether the same NUP98 mark is required outside the TDP-43-variant context. The pore-initiation prediction is that non-phosphorylatable NUP98 preserves import and nuclear TDP-43 while stress granules still form and still contain transport factors, and that phosphomimetic NUP98 impairs import in control neurons before cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies appear. The sequestration prediction is that blocking stress granules restores import whether or not the NUP98 phosphosite is occupied. The broader-stress prediction is that NUP98 phosphorylation and import failure rise together while the non-phosphorylatable allele leaves the import defect intact.

Falsifying observation. The hypothesis is false if NUP98 phosphorylation increases only after import failure and nuclear TDP-43 loss, or if non-phosphorylatable NUP98 leaves import failure, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and neuronal dysfunction unchanged while the stress-granule intervention rescues those phenotypes. Failure of phosphomimetic NUP98 to impair import in control neurons at matched expression is a second falsifier.

Limitations. iPSC-neuron timing does not establish the sequence in ALS tissue or in sporadic disease [S1]. Kinase identity and site occupancy stay assumptions until mapping and allele rescue are finished. A phosphomimetic residue copies a regulated phosphate only approximately. The design does not show how pore phosphorylation and stress-granule sequestration would combine in an intact animal, and it does not validate a treatment.

proposals.title: Stress-triggered phosphorylation of Nup98 at mitotic-disassembly-linked sites initiates nucleocytoplasmic transport failure upstream of TDP-43 mislocalization in TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS motor neurons.
proposals.text:
HYPOTHESIS TITLE: Stress-triggered phosphorylation of Nup98 at mitotic-disassembly-linked sites initiates nucleocytoplasmic transport failure upstream of TDP-43 mislocalization in TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS motor neurons.

MECHANISM AND CAUSAL CHAIN. The proposed initiating event is a pore-intrinsic post-translational modification: in post-mitotic motor neurons exposed to ALS-relevant stress (cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing or repeat-RNA stress), an as-yet-unidentified kinase phosphorylates the nucleoporin Nup98 at residues homologous to those that drive partial nuclear-pore disassembly during mitosis (the existence of such mitotic phosphorylation sites is unverified prior knowledge, not from the packet). The speculative causal chain is: phosphorylated Nup98 weakens pore integrity/barrier function without wholesale disassembly; the Ran gradient and classical NLS-import collapse locally; nuclear TDP-43 is lost; cytoplasmic TDP-43 accumulates and acquires pathological phosphorylation within de-mixed assemblies [S3]; these assemblies and stress granules then sequester transport factors, amplifying the defect [S3, S4]. Under this hypothesis, nucleoporin phosphorylation is the initiating lesion, while transport-factor sequestration into stress granules or TDP-43 assemblies is a downstream amplifier, and TDP-43 phosphorylation itself is a consequence, not a trigger.

SUPPORTED PREMISES (from the packet). (1) TDP-43 pathology physically associates with nuclear-pore and transport components, and disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and transport in experimental systems and ALS tissue, motivating a pore-adjacent mechanism [S1]. (2) A genetic ALS context (C9orf72 repeat expansion) shows RanGAP mislocalization and impaired import in models and patient-derived neurons [S2]. (3) Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can impair import, deplete nuclear TDP-43, and drive cell death independent of conventional stress granules [S3]. (4) Stress granules independently sequester transport factors and impair transport, and perturbing granule assembly modifies transport phenotypes [S4]. These premises establish that transport failure is central in ALS and come in at least two flavors—assembly/sequestration-based (S3, S4) versus pore-associated (S1)—but none identifies or supports a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as causal.

SPECULATIVE BRIDGES (explicit assumptions). Bridge 1: a site-specific Nup98 phosphorylation event actually occurs in ALS neurons; the packet provides no evidence for this. Bridge 2: a disease-relevant kinase can phosphorylate mitotic-type Nup98 sites in post-mitotic neurons; candidate identities (e.g., ectopic CDK-like or stress-activated kinase activity) are unverified prior knowledge and should be discovered empirically, not assumed. Bridge 3: phosphorylation temporally precedes import collapse rather than following it; this is the key untested claim.

ALTERNATIVE EXPLANATIONS. (A) Sequestration-only model: transport factors trapped in stress granules [S4] or TDP-43 assemblies [S3] cause transport failure, and any nucleoporin phosphorylation is a secondary stress response. (B) Direct-binding model: insoluble TDP-43 aggregates mechanically associate with and disrupt pore components, with phosphorylation incidental [S1]. (C) C9orf72-specific mechanisms (repeat RNA, dipeptides) impair transport independently of pore modification [S2].

DISCRIMINATING PRECLINICAL TEST STRATEGY. In iPSC-derived motor neurons from a C9orf72 carrier and a TDP-43-mislocalization induction system, with a live NLS-import reporter: (1) Time course—quantify site-specific phospho-Nup98 (phospho-antibodies plus mass spectrometry), RanGAP mislocalization, and import rate at high temporal resolution. The hypothesis predicts phospho-Nup98 appears before or at the earliest import decline, not after. (2) Necessity—CRISPR knock-in of phospho-dead Nup98 (Ser-to-Ala at candidate disassembly-linked sites): protection from import failure, RanGAP mislocalization, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and cell death after cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing induction supports upstream causality. (3) Sufficiency and directionality—inducible phospho-mimetic Nup98 should reproduce import failure and trigger TDP-43 mislocalization without cytoplasmic assemblies; early recruitment of an NPC-targeted phosphatase should partially rescue even under stress, whereas late dephosphorylation should not, separating initiation from downstream amplification. (4) Orthogonal discrimination from the sequestration alternative—in a parallel arm, stress-granule assembly is blocked (G3BP1/2 deletion or ISRIB; unverified prior knowledge that these suppress granules). If granule blockade fully prevents defects and abolishes phospho-Nup98, the sequestration model dominates; if transport defects persist after granule blockade but are rescued by phospho-dead Nup98, the pore-intrinsic model is favored. (5) In vivo—AAV9 motor-neuron expression of phospho-dead Nup98 in ALS mouse models, tracking phospho-occupancy before symptom onset.

FALSIFYING OBSERVATION. Phospho-dead knock-in neurons show the same timing and magnitude of import failure, RanGAP mislocalization, and nuclear TDP-43 depletion as wild-type after TDP-43 de-mixing or repeat-RNA stress, and phospho-Nup98 signal arises only after import collapse or alongside cell-death markers. This would recast Nup98 phosphorylation as a consequence and affirm the sequestration-based alternatives [S3, S4].

LIMITATIONS. The packet contains no direct evidence that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS, so Bridges 1–3 are assumptions; selected studies predate 2025 and do not cover all ALS subtypes, so the hypothesis is restricted to TDP-43-proteinopathy contexts (C9orf72 and TDP-43-mislocalizing sporadic disease), not all ALS. Pore redundancy among nucleoporins, difficulty achieving site-level knock-in in neurons, and unresolved kinase identity limit inferential strength; results must be interpreted perturbationally, not correlationally.

proposals.title: Atovaquone-induced pyrimidine starvation differentiates oxidative, uridine-salvage-poor AML persisters
proposals.text:
Atovaquone-induced pyrimidine starvation differentiates oxidative, uridine-salvage-poor AML persisters

Hypothesis. Sequential atovaquone after cytarabine will impair complex-III–ubiquinone–DHODH coupling, causing pyrimidine depletion that drives genuine myeloid differentiation and durable clonogenic loss preferentially in oxidative residual AML with low functional uridine-salvage reserve. The effect must occur at achievable unbound marrow exposure. Residual cells are not assumed to be leukemia stem cells.

Supported premises. Cytarabine-resistant cells displayed oxidative-metabolism-associated properties without consistent enrichment for immature, quiescent stem cells [S2]. DHODH inhibition promoted differentiation in experimental AML [S4]. BCL-2 inhibition affected oxidative phosphorylation in ROS-low, functionally defined leukemia stem cells [S1]; this supports analyzing that population separately, not assuming atovaquone selectivity. Venetoclax–azacitidine is an established metabolic comparator, not the repurposing discovery [S3].

Drug-specific evidentiary gap. Atovaquone is recalled as approved for Pneumocystis pneumonia treatment and prevention; that original indication and approval status are unverified prior knowledge here. Reported complex-III inhibition and mammalian DHODH dependence on oxidized ubiquinone are also unverified prior knowledge. The packet establishes neither relevant mammalian pharmacology nor human exposure. Before efficacy interpretation, verify approval/formulation, mammalian target engagement, protein binding, and human pharmacokinetics, then measure unbound plasma and marrow exposure in the model. Audit prior atovaquone–AML and complex-III–DHODH literature. Novelty is provisional and restricted to the post-cytarabine, low-salvage-reserve context and its causal differentiation prediction—not atovaquone activity against AML generally. The speculative bridge is that pyrimidine restriction releases differentiation blockade before generalized energy failure dominates.

Context and stratification. Use paired untreated and cytarabine-residual primary AML from patient-derived models, with independent donors as biological replicates. Low fractional uridine labeling does not establish poor salvage: quantify absolute uridine-to-pyrimidine flux using uptake, tracer kinetics, precursor enrichment, and pool sizes. Measure reserve capacity under graded physiologically relevant uridine concentrations during independently validated DHODH blockade. Define oxidative-state and salvage-reserve thresholds in a separate pilot and lock them before validation. Compare all strata rather than selecting only predicted responders; preferential response in oxidative, low-reserve residuals is the prespecified context prediction.

Controls and endpoints. Compare sequential atovaquone with vehicle, an independently validated DHODH inhibitor, venetoclax–azacitidine, and a viability-matched cytotoxic control. Include normal donor CD34-positive progenitors under matched conditions. Measure early mammalian complex-III activity, ubiquinone redox state, respiration, dihydroorotate/orotate balance, and pyrimidine pools before substantial apoptosis. Record bulk survival separately from differentiation and functional depletion.

Fate attribution. Single-cell trajectories cannot exclude selective survival of pre-existing mature cells. Prospectively index-track initially immature individual blasts and their descendants, using longitudinal imaging followed by morphology and multiple maturation-marker measurements. Count actual immature-to-mature transitions alongside death events; transcriptional trajectories are supplementary evidence. Assess colony formation after washout using equal viable-cell inputs. Analyze ROS-low fractions separately, and measure leukemia-initiating activity by limiting-dilution transplantation: maturation or bulk depletion alone does not demonstrate stem-cell elimination.

Causal discrimination. Initiate rescue before maturation. Supply uridine only when uptake and pyrimidine-pool restoration are demonstrated; poor salvage makes failed supplementation uninterpretable. Otherwise use a biochemically validated respiratory-chain-independent DHODH bypass with an inactive-construct control. The critical prediction is that pyrimidine restoration prevents maturation and clonogenic loss while complex-III inhibition and respiratory suppression persist. Genetic DHODH suppression should phenocopy differentiation with documented pathway engagement. Complex-III inhibition may reduce respiration before pyrimidine depletion; the required temporal ordering is depletion before differentiation, not depletion before any respiratory decline.

Alternatives and falsification. Generalized energy failure, unrelated drug effects, or selective blast killing could explain apparent efficacy. Verified, preemptive pyrimidine restoration that leaves maturation and clonogenic loss unchanged despite persistent respiratory suppression falsifies the proposed pyrimidine-mediated mechanism. Differentiation without preceding pyrimidine depletion also contradicts it. Failure of the prespecified context interaction rejects the claimed oxidative/low-reserve specificity, even if nonspecific activity remains. Activity confined to supraclinical unbound exposure defeats the exposure-constrained proposal.

Limitations. Formulation, protein binding, marrow distribution, donor heterogeneity, and extracellular uridine may prevent translation. Normal cells may share the vulnerability; normal colony formation and long-term hematopoietic engraftment must support a therapeutic window before claiming selectivity. Neither pathway rescue nor xenograft activity establishes clinical benefit, and the frozen packet cannot resolve drug-level feasibility or novelty.

proposals.title: Phosphorylation of FG-nucleoporin NUP98 as an early initiator of nuclear-import failure and nuclear TDP-43 loss in TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS motor neurons
proposals.text:
Phosphorylation of FG-nucleoporin NUP98 as an early initiator of nuclear-import failure and nuclear TDP-43 loss in TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS motor neurons

Hypothesis. In spinal motor neurons with TDP-43 proteinopathy, the pattern common in sporadic ALS, phosphorylation of FG-nucleoporin NUP98 is proposed as an early pore-intrinsic initiating event. The untested prediction is that this modification slows facilitated nuclear import, lowers nuclear TDP-43, and promotes further cytoplasmic TDP-43 accumulation while the pore scaffold stays assembled. Later structural pore injury and sequestration of mobile transport factors are treated as downstream amplifiers. The claim covers this TDP-43-proteinopathy context. A shared initiating phosphorylation step for C9orf72 ALS lies outside the claim.

Supported premises. Insoluble TDP-43 associates with nuclear-pore and transport components, and disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in cell systems, with related pore pathology in ALS tissue [S1]. Cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can form independently of conventional stress granules, mislocalize transport-associated proteins, and accompany import failure, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death [S3]. Those phosphorylated species are TDP-43 rather than a nucleoporin [S3]. Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA is linked to RanGAP mislocalization and impaired nuclear import, and changing transport or repeat-RNA mechanisms modifies model phenotypes [S2]. Cellular stress recruits transport factors into stress granules and impairs transport, and changing stress-granule assembly modifies those phenotypes [S4]. [S3] and [S4] supply sequestration routes, and [S3] shows that conventional stress granules are dispensable for some TDP-43-linked defects.

Speculative bridges. Kinase identity, phosphorylated residues, and the choice of NUP98 are assumptions. Unverified prior knowledge, absent from [S1]-[S4], holds that mitotic proline-directed kinases phosphorylate NUP98 within a multisubunit program that disassembles pores, and that FG repeats help set barrier selectivity. Mitotic disassembly is a mismatch for the claimed scaffold-intact import delay. [S1] reports nucleoporin mislocalization and pore pathology. The bridging assumption is that a persistent neuronal stress kinase places a restricted charge on NUP98 FG-repeat sites in pores already assembled in post-mitotic motor neurons. Absent the mitotic scaffold-release program, that restricted charge is proposed to loosen barrier selectivity and delay TDP-43 import while NUP107 and NUP133 stay at the envelope. This phosphorylation-first order is an untested prediction. [S1] and [S3] support the transport and pore associations alone. Phosphorylation is the candidate initiator. Assembly-driven mislocalization is the candidate downstream response.

Alternative explanations. Stress-granule capture of transport factors can impair import when NUP98 phosphorylation is absent or incidental [S4]. Stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can recruit those factors and block import on their own [S3]. In C9orf72 neurons, RanGAP mislocalization can account for the transport phenotype, with NUP98 phosphorylation a later correlate [S2]. Phosphorylation after failed import, or death from parallel proteostatic stress, would yield the same endpoint.

Discriminating test. Primary cells are human iPSC spinal motor neurons with TARDBP M337V versus isogenic corrected controls. Pre-registered bins are 0, 1, 2, 6, and 12 h after a sublethal sodium arsenite pulse, and only cultures below a pre-specified death threshold are analyzed. Each bin uses pore-fraction mass spectrometry to map NUP98 phosphosites; those sites are outputs and become allele targets only after the map. The same samples score a TDP-43 nuclear-localization-signal reporter, a control SV40-NLS cargo, the nuclear-to-cytoplasmic TDP-43 ratio, G3BP1 granules, TNPO1, RanGAP, and envelope localization of scaffold nucleoporins NUP107 and NUP133. The precedence rule requires NUP98 phosphosite occupancy to rise one bin before either reporter slows, nuclear TDP-43 falls, or TNPO1 is sequestered, with NUP107 and NUP133 still at the envelope. After mapping, near-endogenous phospho-null NUP98 should preserve both reporters and nuclear TDP-43 during arsenite exposure that still forms G3BP1 granules. Phosphomimetic NUP98 in corrected controls, together with G3BP1/2 disruption, should slow both reporters and lower nuclear TDP-43 without granules or sequestration of TNPO1 or RanGAP, while NUP107 and NUP133 stay localized. Matched NUP153 phospho-null and phosphomimetic alleles are the comparator FG-nucleoporin and should lack these effects if the barrier change is NUP98-selective. On phospho-null NUP98, inducible cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies should leave import intact while assemblies remain, favoring a pore-intrinsic step, whereas recovery only after granules disperse would favor sequestration [S4].

Falsifying observation. Falsification in this model is NUP98 occupancy that does not precede import slowing and nuclear TDP-43 loss; envelope loss of NUP107 or NUP133 at first slowing or under phosphomimetic NUP98; unchanged reporters and nuclear TDP-43 after phosphomimetic NUP98 in G3BP1/2-disrupted cells lacking TNPO1 and RanGAP sequestration; a matching NUP153 allele effect; or impaired import on phospho-null NUP98 while assemblies or granules persist. Occupancy rising only after TNPO1 sequestration would mark a downstream correlate.

Limitations. Kinase identity and residue positions stay unknown until the map is complete, and another FG-nucleoporin may be the relevant substrate. Phosphomimetic substitutions approximate charge and can miss kinase-dependent partners. TARDBP M337V and arsenite are protocol choices. iPSC motor neurons omit long aging, glia, and neuromuscular circuitry. A positive result would remain model-specific and would leave the C9orf72 route unresolved [S2]. The design tests a hypothesis.

proposals.title: CDK1-dependent NUP98 phosphorylation initiates nuclear-import failure in sporadic ALS motor neurons
proposals.text:
CDK1-dependent NUP98 phosphorylation initiates nuclear-import failure in sporadic ALS motor neurons

Hypothesis. In C9orf72-expansion-negative, sporadic-ALS-derived motor neurons that initially retain nuclear TDP-43, stress-induced CDK1 phosphorylation of NUP98 reduces its residence at nuclear pores. This intrinsic pore alteration initiates nuclear-import failure, causing nuclear TDP-43 depletion and subsequent neuronal dysfunction. “Initiates” means a proximal trigger of transport failure in this defined context, not the first cause of ALS. Unverified prior knowledge motivates the NUP98/CDK1 nomination; the supplied packet provides no evidence for this pair or a particular phosphorylation site.

Supported premises. TDP-43 pathology can disrupt nucleoporin localization and nucleocytoplasmic transport [S1]. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can inhibit import and accompany nuclear TDP-43 depletion and cell death without conventional stress granules [S3]. Separately, stress granules can sequester transport factors and impair transport [S4]. C9orf72-repeat models demonstrate another route involving altered RanGAP localization and impaired import [S2]. These findings establish transport vulnerability and competing causal routes, but none establishes nucleoporin phosphorylation as an initiating ALS mechanism.

Speculative bridges. The proposed chain requires CDK1 activity to increase before import failure, directly phosphorylate pore-associated NUP98, and weaken its pore retention sufficiently to impair transport. It further assumes that resulting nuclear TDP-43 depletion contributes to functional decline, rather than merely marking injury. Later cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies could amplify transport failure through the mechanisms described in [S1] and [S3]. This feedback is compatible with phosphorylation being upstream initially but downstream during later degeneration; temporal ordering alone would not establish causality.

Discriminating preclinical strategy. Study motor neurons from several independent sporadic-ALS donors and matched unaffected donors, using within-line isogenic perturbations. Follow initially transport-intact neurons during maturation and a calibrated, transient sublethal stress challenge. Serially measure nuclear-import kinetics, endogenous TDP-43 nuclear-to-cytoplasmic distribution, NUP98 pore residence, conventional stress granules, granule-independent TDP-43 assemblies, transport-factor localization, and later evoked firing and survival. Measure export, passive nuclear permeability, cellular energy status, and general stress responses to distinguish import impairment from nonspecific cellular collapse.

First, use endogenous phosphoproteomics in matched cultures to identify NUP98 sites whose phosphorylation rises before pore displacement and import failure. Test whether acute CDK1 suppression prevents these changes and whether purified CDK1 directly phosphorylates the same sites. Freeze the candidate site set before independent validation; absence of an early, directly CDK1-dependent signal would count against the proposed mechanism rather than justify an unrestricted kinase search. Then introduce an inducible, endogenous-level phospho-resistant NUP98 replacement after neuronal differentiation, alongside matched wild-type replacement and wild-type reversion controls. Confirm equivalent baseline abundance, pore incorporation, transport, and neuronal health. Protection must accompany verified suppression of the nominated phosphorylation, not simply reduced stress or altered differentiation.

Test the competing sequestration explanation factorially by blocking NUP98 phosphorylation with or without suppression of conventional stress-granule assembly. Continue measuring granule-independent TDP-43 assemblies because eliminating conventional granules cannot exclude the route in [S3]. Rescue of early import by phospho-resistant NUP98 at comparable initial stress and assembly burden would favor intrinsic pore alteration. Conversely, rescue confined to preventing factor sequestration would favor that alternative. To test the proposed downstream mediator, an independently validated, near-endogenous nuclear-retention TDP-43 intervention should improve neuronal function without correcting NUP98 phosphorylation; otherwise nuclear depletion remains an associated readout rather than a demonstrated mediator.

Falsification and limitations. The central causal claim would be falsified if blocking the nominated NUP98 phosphorylation before onset, while preserving baseline pore incorporation, leaves early import failure and subsequent nuclear TDP-43 depletion unchanged. Phosphorylation consistently appearing only after import failure would additionally contradict its proposed initiating role. Donor heterogeneity, neuronal immaturity, stress-challenge artifacts, and structural effects of phospho-resistant substitutions limit interpretation. Even a positive result would support this mechanism only in the tested sporadic-ALS context, not establish a universal ALS pathway or a validated treatment.

proposals.title: Nup98 phosphorylation as a downstream amplifier of nuclear-import failure after cytoplasmic TDP-43 assembly in ALS/FTD-relevant neurons
proposals.text:
Nup98 phosphorylation as a downstream amplifier of nuclear-import failure after cytoplasmic TDP-43 assembly in ALS/FTD-relevant neurons

The hypothesis is that CDK1 phosphorylation of NPC-retained Nup98 at human T529, S591, S822, and S861 amplifies nuclear-import failure after cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies form in ALS/FTD-relevant neurons. De-mixing of cytoplasmic TDP-43 is the initiating event. The four-site phosphate is a later modification of Nup98 that remains in assembled pores. On this hypothesis, that phosphate adds import failure beyond sequestration, broad stress, and Nup98 exit.

Insoluble TDP-43 aggregates associate with nuclear-pore and transport components. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and transport in experimental cells, and related pore pathology is present in ALS tissue [S1]. Nucleoporin mislocalization in [S1] is distinct from a gating phosphate on pores that retain Nup98, and [S1] names neither a phospho-site nor one sequence for every ALS subtype. Cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can form without conventional stress granules, mislocalize transport proteins, and accompany import failure, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and cell death; phosphorylated TDP-43 in those assemblies is a TDP-43 modification [S3]. C9orf72 repeat RNA is a separate RanGAP-mislocalization route to import failure [S2]. Stress recruits transport factors into stress granules and impairs transport, and changing stress-granule assembly modifies that phenotype [S4]. With [S3], stress granules are dispensable for some TDP-43-linked defects.

Unverified prior knowledge: Nup98 is a central-channel FG-nucleoporin, and mitotic CDK1 phosphorylates T529, S591, S822, and S861 as the envelope breaks down. The bridge is that after assemblies form in post-mitotic neurons, CDK1 writes this four-site mark on NPC-incorporated Nup98 and thereby slows facilitated import enough to worsen TDP-43 re-entry. [S1]-[S4] name neither kinase, residues, nor order. Mass spectrometry of isolated NPCs must show these sites occupied on pore-retained Nup98. If isolated NPCs instead show a different occupied set, the alanine allele is rebuilt to those detected residues before rescue is interpreted. The causal reagent is Nup98 with alanine at exactly those four residues; CDK1 inhibitors stay off that arm because CDK1 has many substrates. Further unverified prior knowledge: FG-nucleoporins exchange over hours to days, whereas neuronal scaffold nucleoporins can last months.

Alternatives can yield the same transport failure. Sequestration in stress granules [S4] or TDP-43 assemblies [S3] can impair import without a required Nup98 phosphate. RanGAP mislocalization can explain import failure in C9orf72-expansion carriers [S2]. Phospho-Nup98 may only report stress-kinase activity, and the mitotic precedent allows phosphate to release Nup98 from the pore, the localization change in [S1].

The test uses human iPSC-derived motor neurons without a C9orf72 expansion, so [S2] is outside the background. Light onset at t = 0 on optoTDP-43 neurons is the trigger; the assumed construct retains an NLS and is meant to form the granule-independent cytoplasmic assemblies in [S3]. Tagged wild-type or four-site alanine Nup98 is expressed from day -10. Assays at 6 h, 24 h, 72 h, and 7 days record assemblies, stress-granule markers, nuclear TDP-43, death, Nup98 rim intensity, NLS-reporter import rate and nucleus/cytoplasm ratio, the tagged fraction of NPC-bound Nup98, and four-site phospho-stoichiometry on isolated NPCs together with rim intensity.

Predicted order is assemblies plus a partial import deficit while four-site NPC occupancy remains below 10% of later stoichiometry (pre-phosphate window, expected 6 h to 24 h), then a further import drop from 72 h through day 7 with rim intensity preserved. Incremental worsening is early minus late import rate in assembly-positive cells. Rescue scoring requires tagged alanine-Nup98 to be at least 50% of NPC-bound Nup98 at 72 h and day 7. Success is recovery of at least half that increment, assemblies within 20% of tag-wild-type pathology, rim intensity within 15% of that control, and at least a 70% drop in four-site NPC stoichiometry. A G3BP-dependent stress-granule block tests [S4]; persistence of NPC phospho-Nup98 and the increment without stress granules aligns the mark with [S3]. Phospho-mimetic Nup98 at the same four sites, without optoTDP-43 light, is a 24 h autonomy test: slower import with retained rim Nup98 and little new insoluble TDP-43 fits an amplifier; rim loss means disassembly; a rapid aggregation wave means an initiator.

Falsifying observations are unoccupied four sites on isolated NPCs while import fails, nuclear TDP-43 falls, and neurons die; phosphate restricted to granule-associated transport factors; alanine-Nup98 at or above 50% NPC incorporation leaving the incremental worsening unchanged while assemblies persist; import scaling with rim loss and no added contribution from stoichiometry on remaining Nup98; or the four-site mark preceding TDP-43 redistribution, including launch of assembly and death by phospho-mimetic Nup98 alone.

Limitations. CDK1, the four residues, optoTDP-43, G3BP dependence, and FG-exchange timing are unverified prior knowledge outside [S1]-[S4]. Phospho-mimetics only approximate phosphate. iPSC motor neurons omit long human aging and do not represent every ALS subtype. Other FG-nucleoporins may compensate, and a misassigned peptide could imitate an NPC signal. The plan is unvalidated.

proposals.title: Teriflunomide-Induced Differentiation in Pyrimidine-Salvage-Limited, Cytarabine-Persistent AML
proposals.text:
Teriflunomide-Induced Differentiation in Pyrimidine-Salvage-Limited, Cytarabine-Persistent AML

Hypothesis: At clinically attainable unbound exposure, teriflunomide will induce durable myeloid differentiation and reduce clonogenicity in cytarabine-persistent AML with limited uridine-salvage capacity, through DHODH-dependent pyrimidine depletion. Salvage-competent AML and normal hematopoietic progenitors should be less affected. This proposes a context-specific differentiation treatment, not an established AML regimen or universal stem-cell therapy.

Unverified prior knowledge requiring confirmation: teriflunomide is approved for relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis, its original indication, and inhibits DHODH, an enzyme involved in de novo pyrimidine synthesis. These drug-specific statements are not established by the supplied packet. Approval details, biochemical selectivity, human unbound exposure, and clinically relevant exposure duration must be checked before translational advancement; no concentration is assumed to be achievable merely because the drug is approved.

Supported premises: DHODH inhibition promoted myeloid differentiation and affected disease-related endpoints in experimental AML systems [S4]. Separately, cytarabine-resistant cells displayed oxidative-metabolism-associated features but were not consistently enriched for immature, quiescent leukemia stem cells [S2]. The ROS-low, BCL-2-associated stem-cell population studied in S1 therefore cannot simply be equated with this residual population [S1, S2]. Venetoclax–azacitidine supplies an established metabolism-focused comparator, not evidence that teriflunomide works [S3]. None of these sources establishes teriflunomide efficacy, its proposed salvage-defined selectivity, or acceptable exposure.

Speculative bridge: a subset of cytarabine-persistent AML may retain substantial de novo pyrimidine dependence while having insufficient extracellular-uridine salvage. In that context, teriflunomide-mediated DHODH inhibition could lower pyrimidine availability sufficiently to release the differentiation blockade before causing generalized cell death. Oxidative metabolism is an enrichment feature to examine, not proof of DHODH dependence. The proposed normal-cell advantage is also an assumption: normal progenitors might instead share the dependency.

Discriminating preclinical strategy: study paired pretreatment and cytarabine-persistent primary AML specimens, alongside normal donor hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells. Maintain physiological uridine and protein conditions rather than artificially favoring de novo synthesis. Define salvage-low and salvage-high groups prospectively using labeled-uridine incorporation and complementary de novo flux measurements, with thresholds fixed before examining drug response. Measure oxidative metabolism separately rather than using it as a surrogate for salvage. Test teriflunomide concentration–time profiles constrained by subsequently verified human free-drug exposure.

Establish temporal ordering through direct DHODH activity measurements, pyrimidine-pool measurements, respiration, viability, morphology, and maturation-marker expression. Genotype-confirmed leukemic progeny should acquire mature morphology and lose serial clonogenicity after washout; marker shifts alone are insufficient. Reduced leukemia-initiating activity would require transplantation evidence and must not be inferred from bulk-cell differentiation. Include vehicle, an orthogonal DHODH perturbation, venetoclax–azacitidine, and identically exposed normal progenitors. Uridine supplementation should restore pyrimidine pools and prevent differentiation if depletion mediates the effect. For stronger drug-specific attribution, develop and validate a catalytically competent, teriflunomide-resistant DHODH construct and test whether it rescues both metabolic and differentiation endpoints. Advance responsive specimens into patient-derived models with measured unbound exposure and marrow toxicity.

Alternatives include off-target cytotoxicity, generalized mitochondrial stress, apparent maturation caused by selective survival of pre-existing mature cells, or expansion of contaminating normal cells. Early target engagement, rescue experiments, single-cell lineage tracking, and leukemic-genotype confirmation distinguish these explanations from genuine differentiation.

Falsification and limitations: confirmed DHODH inhibition and pyrimidine depletion at relevant exposure without durable maturation or reduced clonogenicity in prospectively defined salvage-low residual AML would falsify the central prediction. Persistence of differentiation despite successful drug-resistant-DHODH rescue would reject the proposed mechanism. Comparable injury to normal progenitors would falsify the predicted therapeutic selectivity. Marrow metabolite availability, heterogeneous salvage, achievable exposure, and culture-induced state changes may defeat translation. Even successful preclinical results would establish neither clinical benefit nor eradication of every AML stem-cell population.

proposals.title: Teriflunomide-driven differentiation of uridine-salvage-poor, cytarabine-persistent AML
proposals.text:
Teriflunomide-driven differentiation of uridine-salvage-poor, cytarabine-persistent AML

Hypothesis. At clinically attainable unbound exposure, teriflunomide will induce DHODH-dependent pyrimidine depletion and durable myeloid differentiation in cytarabine-persistent AML blasts with low functional uridine-salvage capacity, reducing their clonogenic recovery while relatively sparing normal hematopoietic progenitors. The intended endpoint is differentiation of viable leukemic cells, not merely bulk-cell killing or presumed leukemia-stem-cell eradication.

Supported premises. DHODH inhibition promoted differentiation and affected disease-related endpoints in experimental AML systems [S4]. Cytarabine-persistent AML cells exhibited oxidative-metabolism-associated features but were not consistently enriched for immature, quiescent leukemia stem cells [S2]. These findings justify studying residual blasts as a distinct population; they do not establish that oxidative metabolism predicts DHODH sensitivity. Likewise, the ROS-low, BCL-2-associated stem-cell dependency described in [S1] cannot be assigned automatically to these residual cells. Venetoclax–azacitidine provides an established energy-metabolism comparator, not the proposed repurposing discovery [S3].

Unverified prior knowledge and speculative bridges. Teriflunomide’s approval for relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis, its DHODH-inhibitory activity, its high protein binding, and DHODH’s role in de novo pyrimidine synthesis are recalled facts requiring independent verification; none is established by this packet. The proposed causal chain is teriflunomide exposure → DHODH inhibition → insufficient pyrimidine production → release of differentiation blockade. The central speculative bridge is that weak utilization of extracellular uridine prevents metabolic compensation in a subset of residual AML. A second necessary assumption is that this dependency permits a differentiation-producing exposure below the threshold that damages normal progenitors. Neither selective exposure nor this residual-disease vulnerability follows directly from [S4].

Discriminating preclinical strategy. Obtain paired pretreatment and cytarabine-persistent primary AML specimens where possible, alongside normal CD34-positive progenitors. After cytarabine washout, prospectively stratify specimens by isotope-measured extracellular-uridine incorporation into pyrimidines, using a prespecified salvage classification independent of drug response. Measure oxidative metabolism separately rather than using it as a surrogate for salvage capacity. Culture all groups under matched, measured uridine and protein-binding conditions, including marrow-like conditions. Establish a concentration range bounded by independently verified human unbound exposure, and measure free drug rather than relying on nominal concentrations.

Measure early DHODH engagement, pyrimidine pools, respiration, ATP, and viability before evaluating later differentiation. Require concordant morphology, maturation-associated immunophenotypes, and persistent loss of clonogenic recovery after washout. Confirm that differentiated cells retain the leukemia genotype. Longitudinal single-cell tracking should distinguish actual maturation from preferential death of immature cells and survival of an already differentiated minority. Compare normal-progenitor colony formation under matched proliferative conditions. Any leukemia-initiating-cell endpoint should be assessed separately through functional transplantation, not inferred from blast maturation.

Mechanistic discrimination and alternatives. Include vehicle, an orthogonal DHODH inhibitor, and venetoclax–azacitidine as a distinct established metabolic comparator [S3]. Genetic DHODH suppression should phenocopy the relevant biochemical and differentiation responses. Uridine supplementation should restore pyrimidine pools and attenuate differentiation; a biochemically validated, catalytically active teriflunomide-resistant DHODH rescue construct, if obtainable, would provide stronger target-specific discrimination. Uridine rescue alone would not prove direct drug–target causality. Competing explanations include reversible cytostasis, nonspecific mitochondrial injury, off-target toxicity, and selection of pre-existing mature cells. These alternatives become more likely if ATP collapse or apoptosis precedes maturation, or if target-specific rescue fails. Advance only exposure-feasible, selective responses into patient-derived models with measured marrow drug and uridine levels.

Falsification and limitations. The hypothesis is falsified if salvage-low residual AML shows confirmed DHODH engagement and pyrimidine depletion at attainable free exposure but no genotype-confirmed differentiation or durable reduction in clonogenic recovery. Comparable normal-progenitor injury or activity confined to unattainable exposure would reject its proposed selective translational window. Physiological uridine availability, marrow interactions, heterogeneous salvage capacity, and differences between experimental and human exposure may eliminate efficacy. Even convincing differentiation would not establish clinical benefit or eradication of leukemia stem cells.

proposals.title: Salvage-Reserve-Stratified Teriflunomide for DHODH-Dependent Differentiation of Post-Cytarabine Residual AML
proposals.text:
Salvage-Reserve-Stratified Teriflunomide for DHODH-Dependent Differentiation of Post-Cytarabine Residual AML

Hypothesis. In post-cytarabine residual AML whose pyrimidine economy is salvage-limited under physiological uridine, teriflunomide at verified unbound marrow exposure will occupy DHODH, lower UTP and CTP, and produce durable myeloid differentiation with reduced leukemia-propagating frequency, while proliferation-matched normal CD34-positive progenitors retain at least a threefold functional margin. Salvage reserve alone defines enrollment. Oxidative and ROS-low states are interaction covariates. Teriflunomide is recalled, as unverified prior knowledge, as an oral agent approved for relapsing multiple sclerosis and as a DHODH inhibitor; approval, protein binding, half-life, marrow distribution, and labeled safety require primary-source confirmation. A literature search for teriflunomide and leflunomide in AML is required before any drug-level novelty claim. If either agent already induces AML differentiation, the incremental claim is only the locked salvage-reserve contrast. Brequinar is recalled, unverified, as a DHODH inhibitor that has entered AML testing. A quantitative free-exposure and occupancy comparison with its clinical pharmacology is a drug-choice gate: clear inferiority of teriflunomide on unbound marrow exposure, occupancy, and tolerability stops or pivots the agent and leaves the salvage-stratified hypothesis intact.

Supported premises. DHODH inhibition promoted myeloid differentiation and affected disease endpoints in experimental AML [S4]; the packet assigns that result to the pathway, and to other inhibitors, rather than to teriflunomide. Cytarabine-residual cells were not consistently enriched for immature quiescent leukemia stem cells, showed mitochondrial and fatty-acid-oxidation features, and changed response when that state was perturbed [S2]. Those data justify residual disease as the setting and oxidative phenotype as a covariate. They do not show salvage limitation. Often ROS-low, BCL-2-high leukemia stem cells were sensitive to BCL-2 inhibition through reduced oxidative phosphorylation [S1]. Venetoclax–azacitidine altered leukemia-stem-cell TCA-cycle and oxidative-phosphorylation metabolism and is an established metabolic comparator [S3]. Repeating that regimen is outside this proposal. [S3] supports stem-cell metabolic effects and does not establish differentiation as its endpoint.

Speculative bridges. No packet evidence shows residual AML to be salvage-limited, or oxidative metabolism to equal de novo pyrimidine demand. The assumptions are that a measurable donor subset cannot refill pyrimidines from physiological uridine, that partial depletion releases differentiation ahead of generalized killing, and that normal progenitors keep the stated margin at the same free exposure. Expression of DHODH, UMPS, and nucleoside transporters versus chemotherapy state is only a plausibility screen.

Operational rules. In a training cohort, lock three metabolic cutoffs with no reference to drug response: de novo-to-salvage isotope-flux ratio at least 3:1, UTP plus CTP at or below 50 percent of the paired pretreatment median, and uridine refill of nucleotide pools below a cutoff taken from that training distribution at physiological uridine. Apply the locked rules to held-out residual donors and paired pretreatment samples. Continue only if at least 20 percent of at least 20 independent residual donors qualify; lower prevalence is a feasibility stop. Durable differentiation means, after 72 hours of exposure and 96 hours of washout at equal viable leukemic input, a concurrent at least twofold rise in CD11b/CD14-positive fraction and mean fluorescence plus a blinded morphologic maturation score in genotype-confirmed leukemic cells, with at least 50 percent reductions in colony output and limiting-dilution propagating frequency. Selectivity fails if proliferation-matched normal CD34 long-term culture-initiating cells or competitive repopulation fall by at least 50 percent, or if the normal-colony IC50 to AML differentiation EC50 ratio is below 3, at protein-adjusted, pharmacokinetics-capped exposure.

Validation. Gate A confirms pharmacology and requires modeled free marrow trough to reach the occupancy linked to differentiation-range pyrimidine depletion, benchmarked against brequinar. Gate B is the locked-cutoff prevalence pilot with salvage-enzyme measurements. Gate C tests held-out salvage-limited versus salvage-replete residual AML and paired pretreatment cells against matched normal CD34 cells in stromal coculture, resting and proliferation-matched, inside the exposure ceiling. Occupancy and nucleotide depletion are recorded before maturation, apoptosis, and proliferation. Comparators are vehicle, an orthogonal DHODH inhibitor, DHODH knockdown, venetoclax–azacitidine [S3], and a fatty-acid-oxidation or complex-I inhibitor matched for viability. Gate D is a patient-derived xenograft with controlled uridine and nutrients, measured plasma and marrow exposure, occupancy-versus-maturation correlation, limiting-dilution propagation, and normal competitive repopulation. Mediator proof requires documented restoration of UTP and CTP by uridine and a catalytically functional teriflunomide-resistant DHODH construct. Time-resolved tracking of initially immature leukemic cells separates maturation from selective loss of immature cells.

Falsification and stops. Biological disconfirmation is verified occupancy and pyrimidine depletion at achievable free exposure without the prespecified maturation and propagation changes; differentiation that persists after documented nucleotide-pool restoration; equal maturation and propagating-frequency effects in held-out salvage-replete cells at matched occupancy; or a fatty-acid-oxidation or complex-I inhibitor matching those effects at equal viability. Feasibility stops, kept separate from mechanism, are prevalence below 20 percent, free trough below the occupancy threshold, or failure to reach marrow exposure. Prior art that already shows the same salvage-stratified result removes the incremental claim.

Limitations. Donor heterogeneity, culture-conditioned salvage, marrow nutrients, and xenograft artifacts limit inference. The cited studies are model- and cohort-specific. Positive preclinical results would justify further study only.

proposals.title: Teriflunomide-driven differentiation of uridine-salvage-low, differentiation-arrested AML
proposals.text:
Teriflunomide-driven differentiation of uridine-salvage-low, differentiation-arrested AML

Hypothesis. Low functional uridine salvage will predict greater teriflunomide-induced, DHODH-dependent differentiation than high salvage in differentiation-arrested AML, at human-attainable unbound exposure that preserves normal-progenitor function. Cytarabine persistence is a separately tested context, not an assumed cause of salvage deficiency. The intended outcomes remain viable leukemic-cell maturation and durable loss of clonogenic recovery—not nonspecific killing or presumed stem-cell eradication.

Evidence and context correction. DHODH inhibition promoted differentiation in experimental AML [S4]. However, neither teriflunomide efficacy nor salvage-based selection follows from that finding. Cytarabine-resistant cells exhibited oxidative-metabolism-associated features, without an established salvage defect [S2]. Therefore, include untreated, de novo salvage-low AML alongside persistent disease. The ROS-low/BCL-2-associated population in [S1] must remain distinct; venetoclax–azacitidine is an established metabolic comparator [S3], not the repurposing discovery.

Novelty and pharmacological uncertainty. This proposes an approved-drug implementation with prospective salvage stratification, not discovery of DHODH-driven AML differentiation [S4]. Unverified prior knowledge: teriflunomide is an oral drug approved for relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis, inhibits DHODH, and is highly protein-bound; DHODH participates in de novo pyrimidine synthesis. Recollections about dedicated clinical DHODH-inhibitor programs and comparative immunosuppressive/off-target liabilities also require verification. Teriflunomide is chosen for its recalled non-AML approval, not demonstrated superiority over purpose-built inhibitors. The speculative bridges are that salvage capacity becomes rate-limiting under marrow conditions and creates a leukemia-versus-normal therapeutic window.

Pilot and locked population definition. Before efficacy testing, screen 12 paired pretreatment/post-cytarabine specimens after cytarabine washout. Prespecify a four-hour [U-13C9,15N2]uridine pulse at 5 µM total uridine, 50% labeled, measuring enrichment-corrected fractional UTP labeling: below 10% defines salvage-low, at least 20% defines salvage-high, and intermediate specimens remain unclassified. These are proposed operational cutoffs, not established biomarkers; report absolute incorporation, UTP pools, viability, cycling, and frequency uncertainty. Five micromolar is an assay setting, not a claimed marrow concentration. Require at least three salvage-low residual donors before expanding that arm. Subsequently use an independent pretreatment/persistent × salvage-low/high design, separating salvage effects from treatment history.

Quantitative exposure gate. Feasibility cannot be inferred from total plasma concentration. Before differentiation testing, lock E in nM: a conservative, independently verified human steady-state unbound trough at approved dosing. Measure C80, the free concentration producing 80% cellular DHODH inhibition, and test 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, and 1.0 times E under measured binding conditions. Advance only if C80 ≤ E, UTP falls at least 30%, and normal-progenitor colony output remains at least 80% of vehicle. Absolute exposure values are unavailable in this packet and must be verified rather than guessed. Repeat under measured marrow-like uridine conditions and compare potency/exposure margins with a verified, available clinical DHODH inhibitor.

Locked differentiation and selectivity endpoints. After seven treatment days, require a 20-percentage-point increase in viable leukemia-genotype-positive CD11b-positive cells coexpressing CD14 or CD15, corroborated by blinded mature morphology. Require at least 50% fewer colonies during a 14-day drug-free assay after washout, seeded with equal viable leukemic inputs. Validate the proposed marker panel independently. Longitudinal single-cell tracking must distinguish maturation from selective survival of pre-existing mature cells. Measure early DHODH activity, pyrimidine pools, ATP, respiration, apoptosis, and viability; compare matched-cycling normal CD34-positive progenitors. Any leukemia-initiating-cell claim requires separate functional transplantation.

Causal discrimination and alternatives. Include vehicle, high-salvage AML, orthogonal DHODH inhibition, genetic DHODH suppression, and venetoclax–azacitidine [S3]. Uridine supplementation should restore nucleotide pools and attenuate maturation; this is a pathway control, not the novel contribution or sufficient proof of direct targeting. A catalytically validated teriflunomide-resistant DHODH construct, if obtainable, provides stronger discrimination. Reversible cytostasis, off-target mitochondrial injury, and selection of mature cells remain alternatives, especially if ATP collapse or apoptosis precedes differentiation. Advance only passing specimens into patient-derived models with measured marrow drug and uridine.

Falsification and limitations. Confirmed engagement and depletion at ≤ E without the specified maturation and durable clonogenic response falsify the proposed relationship in the tested salvage-low context. Equivalent responses in independently validated salvage-high cells undermine salvage-based selection. Failure of the pilot gate closes the persistence extension without disproving the broader context. Unattainable exposure or comparable normal injury rejects the translational window. Marrow compensation, heterogeneous salvage, and systemic immune effects may defeat selectivity; immunodeficient models cannot establish immune safety. Differentiation alone establishes neither clinical benefit nor stem-cell eradication.

proposals.title: Stress-triggered phosphorylation of Nup98 at mitotic-disassembly-linked GLFG-repeat S/T-P sites initiates nucleocytoplasmic transport failure upstream of TDP-43 mislocalization in TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS motor neurons.
proposals.text:
HYPOTHESIS TITLE: Stress-triggered phosphorylation of Nup98 at mitotic-disassembly-linked GLFG-repeat S/T-P sites initiates nucleocytoplasmic transport failure upstream of TDP-43 mislocalization in TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS motor neurons.

MECHANISM AND CAUSAL CHAIN. The proposed initiating event is a pore-intrinsic post-translational modification in post-mitotic motor neurons: ALS-relevant stress activates a proline-directed kinase that phosphorylates Nup98 at GLFG-domain S/T-P serine/threonine motifs — the same site class that is phosphorylated to drive partial NPC disassembly during mitosis. Mitotic Nup98 phosphorylation is documented in prior literature (recalled from training data, not supplied by the packet); it is therefore reclassified from a speculative bridge to a known biological premise about mitosis, with published mitotic phospho-proteomic maps supplying residue-level annotation from which candidate GLFG-repeat serines should be selected (not invented here). The remaining speculative causal chain is: phosphorylated Nup98 weakens the FG-permeability barrier without wholesale disassembly; the Ran gradient and classical NLS-import collapse locally; nuclear TDP-43 is lost; cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixes and acquires pathological phosphorylation within persistent assemblies [S3]; those assemblies and stress granules sequester transport factors, amplifying the defect [S3, S4]. Nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates; sequestration is a downstream amplifier; TDP-43 phosphorylation is a consequence.

SUPPORTED PREMISES FROM THE PACKET. (1) TDP-43 pathology associates with nuclear-pore/transport components and disrupts nucleoporin localization and transport in experimental systems and ALS tissue [S1]. (2) C9orf72 repeat expansion causes RanGAP mislocalization and impaired import in models and patient-derived neurons [S2]. (3) Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies impair import, deplete nuclear TDP-43, and drive cell death independently of conventional stress granules [S3]. (4) Stress granules sequester transport factors and impair transport; perturbing granule assembly modifies phenotypes [S4]. None establishes nucleoporin phosphorylation as causal.

PRIOR-KNOWLEDGE PREMISE AND REMAINING SPECULATIVE BRIDGES. Documented prior-literature premise (not packet): mitotic Nup98 phosphorylation by CDK1-like activity occurs during NPC disassembly. Bridge 1 (now narrowed): interphase ALS-relevant stress ectopically re-phosphorylates those mitotic-type GLFG sites in post-mitotic neurons — no packet or packet-external evidence establishes this for ALS. Bridge 2: the interphase kinase is individually testable; explicit candidates are CDK5 (proline-directed, highly expressed in post-mitotic neurons) and stress-activated ERK/MAPK, both capable of S/T-P phosphorylation (CDK5 and MAPK neuronal roles are unverified prior knowledge; their activation under ALS stress is an assumption). Bridge 3: phosphorylation temporally precedes import collapse.

ALTERNATIVE EXPLANATIONS. (A) Sequestration-only: transport factors trapped in granules [S4] or TDP-43 assemblies [S3] cause failure; phosphorylation is a secondary stress response. (B) Direct-binding: insoluble TDP-43 mechanically disrupts pore components; phosphorylation incidental [S1]. (C) C9orf72-specific repeat-RNA or dipeptide mechanisms impair transport without pore modification [S2].

DISCRIMINATING PRECLINICAL TEST STRATEGY. System: iPSC-derived motor neurons (C9orf72 carrier and TDP-43-de-mixing induction) with live NLS-import reporter and pre-stress baseline measurements of import rate, mRNA export, FG-barrier function, and pore ultrastructure.
1. Site nomination and reagent validation. Enumerate Nup98 GLFG S/T-P serines against published mitotic phospho-site maps; generate phospho-antibodies to top candidates; validate specificity by (i) signal loss in phospho-dead knock-in, (ii) signal gain in phospho-mimetic knock-in, (iii) LC-MS/MS confirmation. Pre-register detection limit and occupancy threshold (e.g., ≥5% occupancy by MS or phospho-signal ≥3σ above phospho-dead background).
2. Temporal precedence (primary discriminator). Sampling every 5 minutes from stress onset for ≥6 hours, quantifying phospho-Nup98, import rate, and granule burden at each interval. Pre-registered rule: the pore-intrinsic model requires phospho-Nup98 detectable at or before the first time point at which import declines ≥15% from baseline, and before or at earliest detectable granule nucleation.
3. Necessity with baseline controls. Introduce single-site (not multi-site) phospho-dead edits at individually nominated GLFG serines, including at least one kinase-docking-disruptive edit. Before stress induction, require baseline import, mRNA export, and pore function indistinguishable from wild-type; clones with perturbed baselines are excluded as uninterpretable.
4. Sufficiency and directionality. Inducible phospho-mimetic Nup98 should reproduce import decline and trigger TDP-43 mislocalization without cytoplasmic assemblies; early NPC-targeted phosphatase recruitment should partially rescue under stress, late recruitment should not.
5. Sequestration discrimination — revised. Temporal precedence (step 2), not pharmacological granule blockade, is the primary discriminator, because ISRIB or G3BP1/2 deletion may blunt upstream stress rather than only removing granules. Orthogonal granule-disruption approaches are secondary; residual granule burden is quantified in every arm, and arms with persistent residual granules are weighted as unable to cleanly separate models.
6. In vivo specification with quantitative rules. Contexts matching hypothesis scope: (a) TDP-43 proteinopathy — rNLS8 or equivalent inducible TDP-43 ΔNLS line (not SOD1); (b) C9orf72 repeat-expansion mice. AAV9 hSyn or ChAT promoter at pre-defined dose and delivery age; pre-symptomatic sampling (e.g., P30, P60, P90). Decision rule: within the same animal, phospho-Nup98 must be detectable ≥1 sampling interval before RanGAP mislocalization or import decline.

FALSIFYING OBSERVATION. If, at the pre-registered temporal resolution and occupancy thresholds, phospho-Nup98 first appears after or simultaneously with import collapse in both contexts, and single-site phospho-dead knock-ins with verified-unperturbed baseline show identical timing and magnitude of import failure, RanGAP mislocalization, and nuclear TDP-43 depletion as wild-type, the hypothesis is falsified and Nup98 phosphorylation is recast as a downstream stress response supporting sequestration or direct-binding alternatives [S1, S3, S4].

LIMITATIONS. The packet contains no direct evidence that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS; Bridges 1–3 remain assumptions. Mitotic Nup98 phosphorylation is documented prior literature, not packet evidence. The scope is restricted to TDP-43-proteinopathy contexts (C9orf72 and TDP-43-mislocalizing sporadic disease), not all ALS. Nup98 is dosage-sensitive; single-site edits retain baseline-perturbation risk, addressed but not eliminated by step 3. Phospho-antibody specificity for low-abundance neuronal targets is a known pitfall addressed by knock-in gain/loss-of-signal validation. Results must be interpreted perturbationally, not correlationally.

proposals.title: Nup98 phosphorylation as a downstream amplifier of nuclear-import failure after cytoplasmic TDP-43 assembly in ALS/FTD-relevant neurons
proposals.text:
Nup98 phosphorylation as a downstream amplifier of nuclear-import failure after cytoplasmic TDP-43 assembly in ALS/FTD-relevant neurons
